newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE oil products up tentatively before IPE expiry.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products up tentatively before IPE expiry.

text.p: NWE oil products all firmed on Monday morning by about $1, heating oil gains rather muted ahead of the expiry of May IPE futures at midday, dealers said.

Prompt gas oil futures gained by almost $1 a tonne, but weaker heating oil premiums wiped out most of the gains. Offers softened to IPE May +50 cents in the final hours of the May contract which expires at 1100 GMT today.

Most talk was of the likely size of the delivery against expiring May futures contract. Some saw a delivery volume approaching 500,000 tonnes, but most believed it would be substantially less as much of the transfer had already been done via exchange for physical (EFP) deals.
"It seems up to 500,000 tonnes of EFPs were done between (two large traders) on Friday," one barge trader said.

Gasoline barges were slightly firmer, Rotterdam Eurograde offered at $199 fob, $1 higher than at Friday's close. Swaps were up more sharply with June gaining almost $2 a tonne. Traders said the quiet physical market was likely to lag swaps until NYMEX unleaded futures opened this afternoon.
"People are just being a bit cautious for the moment," one trader said.
High sulphur fuel oil was up $1 a tonne, trading at $86 and $87 fob Rotterdam. Late morning offers were at $87.
Bunker demand was limited, initial indications suggesting traded volume would be below 10,000 tonnes.
